 Texas will welcome in-state foe Houston to Mike A. Myers Stadium and Soccer Field on Friday night as the teams hope to advance in the NCAA Tournament with a first round win. 
 Houston and Texas will meet Friday in a matchup that brings together two Texas programs looking to make their mark on the women’s college soccer schedule. The contest will provide an opportunity for both sides to build momentum, with defensive organization, midfield possession and finishing chances likely to play important roles. Texas will look to use its athleticism and attacking depth to create opportunities, while Houston will aim to disrupt the Longhorns’ rhythm and capitalize on chances in transition. With both teams eager to deliver a strong performance, execution in the final third could ultimately determine the outcome.

 Houston comes into Friday’s first-round matchup with an overall record of 11-5-4 and a No. 23 national ranking, earning the first NCAA Tournament appearance in program history. The Cougars will be looking to rebound from a 1-0 loss to Baylor in the Big 12 Tournament quarterfinals on November 9. Texas, meanwhile, owns a 9-5-7 record and secured the No. 5 seed after reaching the SEC Tournament championship game. The Longhorns defeated top-ranked Vanderbilt 2-1 during their postseason run before falling to South Carolina 4-1 in the final.
 Houston has seen balanced offensive production throughout the season, with 14 different players finding the back of the net. Sophomore Bailey Cate leads the Cougars with eight goals, while the team’s goalkeepers have combined for 10 shutouts. Four players earned All-Big 12 recognition, including first-team defender Ella Morgan.
 Texas counters with an attack led by Amalia Villarreal, who has eight goals, and Ava McDonald, who has seven. The Longhorns have recorded 34 goals and 28 assists this season while collecting eight clean sheets.
 The teams have split some recent success, with Houston winning their most recent meeting 4-1 in August 2025. However, Texas holds a 7-2 advantage in the all-time series and will benefit from playing at home. Friday’s winner will advance to the second round of tournament play, taking on either Purdue or Southern Illinois.
